checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path truelearner/Cargo.toml -p truelearner-body --lib --test engine --test attachment --test calibration --test physics

findings: Normal Body::step execution now derives one reaction from the retained physical moment and applies its edits after ordinary transmission and before releasing the moment.
All six shared scenarios pass through the new adapter unchanged: quiet, local action, distance rejection, learned reuse, checkpoint replay, and deterministic variants.
The old black-box oracle, kernel, attachment, calibration, observer-purity, distance, and checkpoint controls remain green.
The broader unchanged body-law frontier improved from 13 passing and 15 failing to 17 passing and 11 failing; no previously passing law regressed.
On this host, the warmed primitive-wave benchmark measured 42.83 ns minimum, 43.67 ns median, and 44.20 ns maximum across nine samples of five million waves.
residual_uncertainty: The primitive-wave benchmark measures admitting one input and running one single-junction physical moment; it does not measure a learned action wave or a large learned body.

Eleven unchanged higher laws still fail around connected competition, outcome availability, and recursive membership, so the result supports the shared adapter contract but not complete compact-body equivalence.
Live-return discovery currently scans link memory when evaluating a possible consequence; large learned-body scaling remains unverified.
